objective: Exploratory census under a frozen contract: two rings sharing one contact cell (a figure-eight), every non-contact cell updating by its ring's elementary rule and the contact combining the two rings' proposals by a two-input law, so that each ring feeds the other through the contact. For every rule class, every two-input combiner and declared ring sizes, find exactly (by iterating the finite dynamics until its maps repeat) at which lags the contact binds both rings, whether the binding persists at every lag, and how feedback changes the listening model's answer (only parities bind).
status: Supported 2026-11-08 (exploratory): of 128,128 shared-contact configurations, exact at every lag, 44 bind both rings at every lag, all with a parity combiner (at lag 1 binding needs a parity and neither rule canalizing at its centre); sharing breaks 13,068 of the 13,104 parity bindings a listening contact keeps forever and rescues 8; 53 non-parity configurations bind from some lag on (H1 and H2 fail). Controls passed.
title: Rings that share their contact cell
